name: Ikulu
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Seitz, Gitte 1993. Ikulu: Untersuchungen zu einer zentralnigerianischen Klassensprache (Hamburg). Not online. Blench 2006 Kulu wordlist WAS read: phonology section covers vowels/consonants/tones only, no stress statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x reference list for ikul1238 (7 refs: Seitz 1993 x2, Shimizu 1996, Williamson 1973, Williamson & Shimizu 1968 BCCW, Blench 2006, Gunn 1956 ethnographic).

sources.citation: Shimizu, Kiyoshi. 1996. A Kulu vocabulary and fragments of Kulu grammatical structures. AFLANG Web Journal (June 1996). Tokyo: AFLANG / TUFS. [web text, archived at web.archive.org 2004-10-12]
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Nothing. Part One §1 Phonology covers vowels (1.1), consonants (1.2), tones (1.3: 'There are three distinct tone levels...'; composite/falling tones; tone-bearing sonorants), phonological changes (1.4), intonation (1.5). Preface §4: 'It has three distinct level tones, which are sometimes contracted to falling tones.' No occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent' in the whole document.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019/2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 4th ed. Entry 268 Kulu.
sources.note: Nothing; bibliographic only: 'Source(s) Shimizu (n.d.); Moser (n.d.); Wordlists: Blench (2016); Grammars: Seitz (1993), Shimizu (1996)'.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2017. Nominal affixes and number marking in the Plateau languages of Central Nigeria. In John R. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs (Niger-Congo Comparative Studies 1), 107-172. Berlin: Language Science Press. [Kulu §2.1, pp. 113-120]
sources.note: Nothing; treats Kulu noun-class prefixes (re-analysis of Moser 1982 / Seitz 1993); notes CV prefixes may bear one of three tone levels in Kulu. States that no new data on Northwest Plateau has been published apart from Moser 1982 (analysed in Seitz 1993) and Shimizu 1996.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. The Kulu language of Central Nigeria and its affinities [Kulu wordlist paper]. Draft ms. dated 3 January 2006, Cambridge: Mallam Dendo. 33 pp. (compiles Moser 1982 ms wordlist, Blench 1981 field data, Shimizu 1996)
sources.note: Nothing. §3 Phonology ('based on rapid observations... tentative'): 3.1 vowels (7-8), 3.2 consonants, 3.3 Tones p.2: 'Kulu has three level tones and at least two glide tones.' No stress statement anywhere.

sources.citation: Seitz, Gitte. 1993. Ikulu: Untersuchungen zu einer zentralnigerianischen Klassensprache. Magisterarbeit, Universität Hamburg. 72 pp.

sources.note: The only grammar sketch of Ikulu beyond Shimizu's web notes (Glottolog hhtype grammar_sketch, 72 pp, German); a Hamburg Afrikanistik thesis under Gerhardt would normally include a Phonologie chapter with a Ton/Akzent subsection — the one place a stress/accent statement for Ikulu could exist. Glottolog/MPI-EVA hold a scan.
